title: Wells Share One Scoop of Water

scenes.tts: Pond S2 has twenty qPCR wells. Every one is negative. Is the species gone? Not yet. A false negative is a miss. The organism or its DNA is present, and nothing amplifies. To see why, follow the DNA from the pond to the well.
scenes.visual: A pond and twenty wells in a grid; every well fills with a zero while a question mark sits in the pond; the question mark turns into DNA dots that the wells missed.
scenes.narration: Pond S2 has twenty qPCR wells. Every one is negative. Is the species gone? Not yet. A false negative is a miss. The organism or its DNA is present, and nothing amplifies. To see why, follow the DNA from the pond to the well.

scenes.tts: Think of the survey as three nets, each with holes. First, DNA must be in the water you scoop. We set that chance at zero point six. Second, the extraction must capture it. In a wild pig study in central Texas, that chance was zero point four nine. Third, a qPCR run must amplify it. That chance was zero point three eight. We borrow both as illustrative estimates from one species and one region. Each net can let the signal slip through.
scenes.caption: Think of the survey as three nets, each with holes. First, DNA must be in the water you scoop. We set that chance at 0.60. Second, the extraction must capture it. Each net can let the signal slip through.
scenes.visual: Three nets stacked, each labelled with its chance; DNA dots fall and are caught at the nets one by one.

scenes.tts: Start with the lab. One run misses with probability zero point six two. All five runs miss with probability zero point zero nine two. So five runs amplify captured DNA with probability zero point nine zero eight. Add the capture step, and two extractions detect with probability zero point six nine two.
scenes.caption: Start with the lab. One run misses with probability 0.62. All five runs miss with probability 0.092. So five runs amplify captured DNA with probability 0.908. Add the capture step, and two extractions detect with probability 0.692.
scenes.visual: One water sample feeds two extractions of five wells; the miss chance of one well becomes the miss chance of five, then the detection chance of the lab side.
scenes.narration: Start with the lab. One run misses with probability 0.62. All five runs miss with probability 0.092. So five runs amplify captured DNA with probability 0.908. Add the capture step, and two extractions detect with probability 0.692.

scenes.tts: Now the scoop. Zero point six times zero point six nine two gives zero point four one five. That is the chance one water sample detects an occupied pond. Could more wells fix it? Even perfect lab work gives no more than zero point six. If the scoop held no DNA, no number of runs will find it.
scenes.caption: Now the scoop. 0.6 times 0.692 gives 0.415. That is the chance one water sample detects an occupied pond. Could more wells fix it? Even perfect lab work gives no more than 0.6. If the scoop held no DNA, no number of runs will find it.
scenes.visual: A bar from zero to one: the scoop chance, the lab share inside it, then the lab share grows to the scoop ceiling and stops.
scenes.narration: Now the scoop. 0.6 times 0.692 gives 0.415. That is the chance one water sample detects an occupied pond. Could more wells fix it? Even perfect lab work gives no more than 0.6. If the scoop held no DNA, no number of runs will find it.

scenes.tts: Only another independent water sample attacks the forty percent chance that the scoop holds no DNA. Two samples both miss an occupied pond with probability zero point three four two. Start from a prior occupancy of zero point two. Bayes rule then gives seven point nine percent that the pond is still occupied. The team stops only at five percent or below, so it samples again. A third negative sample gives four point eight percent, just under the line.
scenes.caption: Only another independent water sample attacks the 40% chance that the scoop holds no DNA. Two samples both miss an occupied pond with probability 0.342. Start from a prior occupancy of 0.2. Bayes' rule then gives 7.9% that the pond is still occupied. The team stops only at 5% or below, so it samples again. A third negative sample gives 4.8%, just under the line.
scenes.visual: Bars of the chance the pond is occupied: the prior, after two negative samples, after three; a stop line at five percent.

scenes.tts: Now count the twenty wells as twenty independent tries. That is pseudoreplication. It gives two point three percent, and you would stop on an error in the model, not on evidence. Even the honest numbers rest on choices. The zero point six, the prior, and the five percent are ours. Changing them can change the decision. Wells from one sample share its scoop. Only new water samples count as new tries.
